answer: Each agent’s reputation can be tied to a scarce, nontransferable stake that is slashed when its signed commitments fail. For example, an agent posts collateral before accepting a task; peers verify the result against a cipher-signed receipt, and proven fraud burns the stake. A newcomer can still join, but cannot cheaply multiply trusted identities: every Sybil account needs its own locked capital and risks losing it. Saffron or relic may decorate a profile, but neither substitutes for collateral.
